title: [Mouse Without Borders] Use policy IP mapping rules without user rules

proposed_comments.title: Pass the intentional null test value without redundant suppression

confidence.rationale: Real MSTest regression cases and exact helper source passed a focused warnings-as-errors compile; null remains null.

proposed_comments.body:
### Pass the intentional null test value without redundant suppression

**Severity:** `low` (non-blocking test clarity)

The production helper is compiled without nullable annotations, so this call does not require `!`. Passing `policyMappings` directly keeps the `[DataRow(null, ...)]` case visible without implying that the helper rejects it.

Do not coalesce the value to `string.Empty`: that would stop exercising actual null input. No production signature or runtime behavior change is requested. The exact test class and two production helpers compiled with warnings as errors, and all 13 cases passed, including both actual-null rows, with these suppressions removed.

```suggestion
        var mappings = SocketStuff.GetName2IpMappingLines(policyMappings, "PEER 192.0.2.1");
```
